question: Is a continuous 0-100 per-domain score meaningful under the locked domain-split architecture, or is it manufactured precision on top of a validated 2-tier categorical result?
scope: Investigation only. No production scoring logic built, no production artifact or code modified. Reads the locked domain-split artifacts.

candidates.POP: (a) population min-max of distance to the healthy-tier centroid, in the model's own scaled space, normalized within age band (Approach A) or pooled (Approach B). RELATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION — tested for completeness only; shipping it would reintroduce the relative-ranking trap the project has avoided everywhere else.
candidates.ABS: (b) Euclidean distance to a fixed absolute anchor built from the domain's own benchmark thresholds, in benchmark units. Uses no fitted scaler and no population statistic.
candidates.MEMB: (c) inverse-distance membership across the model's own centroids — the continuous reading of the validated partition itself.
candidates.BENCH: REFERENCE CEILING, not a candidate: share of the domain's own out-of-model benchmarks cleared. Shows how much ordinal signal is available in principle.

dti.floor_source: MAS TDSR ceiling 55% — the regulatory limit

risk_age_deviation.ideal_source: structural zero of the derived quantity (equity_pct minus the 100-minus-age target)
risk_age_deviation.floor_source: +/-50pp from target — REASONED, no benchmark exists

life_coverage_ratio.ideal_source: LIA Protection Gap Study 2022 9x income (band 5: 5x, per SYNTHETIC_IDEALS)

absolute_anchor_coverage_gap: Insurance's ABS anchor covers 2 of its 3 clustering features. `insurance_spend_ratio` has NO benchmark anywhere in this project — it is in no BENCHMARKS list and SYNTHETIC_IDEALS never held a value for it. A sensitivity variant adds it on a reasoned, explicitly uncited 10%-of-income anchor.

insurance_ABS_spend_ratio_sensitivity.why: insurance_spend_ratio is a clustering feature with no benchmark anywhere in the project. Adding it to the absolute anchor requires inventing a threshold, so the effect of doing so is measured rather than assumed.

anchor_used.source: '~10% of income on insurance' rule of thumb — REASONED, UNCITED, no SG benchmark exists

insurance_ABS_spend_ratio_sensitivity.additional_caveat: Treating a HIGHER premium spend as healthier is itself questionable — overspending on premiums is a real financial-health problem, so this feature is not monotonically 'more is better' the way coverage is.

step4_alternative_tier_plus_layer1.construction: 1 point per domain landing in its healthy tier (Banking Stable / Investment On Track / Insurance Covered) + 1 point per Layer 1 checklist flag passed (has_investments, hospitalisation_coverage, income_protection_coverage). Total 0-6, rendered as 0-100.
step4_alternative_tier_plus_layer1.caveat: Layer 1 is 3 of its 4 features here — `dependants` is not present in the synthetic dataset. Layer 1's real thresholds are also personalised by salary and age in production, which this flat version does not model.
